name: Real estate agency
description: A real estate agency: property listings for sale and to let, the agents, references from sellers and buyers and clients' questions, with facts about licences and memberships, the areas covered, commission and valuations.

questions.question: Which licences, registrations or professional memberships do you hold?
questions.help: Only what you actually hold today, with the name of the body. Whether a licence is required, and whether it must appear on the site, depends on your country – check it.

questions.question: Which towns, districts or regions do you cover?
questions.help: As buyers and sellers search for them, e.g. "Prague 4, 5 and 10, and Prague-West district".

questions.question: How is your commission set, and who pays it?
questions.help: A plain statement, e.g. "paid by the seller, agreed in the brokerage contract". Rules on who may be charged differ by country – check them.

questions.question: Do you offer property valuations? On what terms?
questions.help: For example "free market estimate for sellers" or "official valuation by a certified valuer for a fee". Leave it empty if you do not.

questions.question: In which languages can clients deal with you?
Since which year has the agency been in business?

audit.message: Add your current listings – buyers and tenants come for them.
No listing has changed for three months – hide sold or let properties and check prices and statuses.
Introduce your agents with a photo and direct contact – clients deal with a person.
Say how your commission works and who pays it – clients want to know before they call.
Publish a privacy policy page – enquiries about properties collect personal data; check what your law requires.

claude: Buyers and tenants come for the listings, sellers for proof that the agency sells in their area – so the current listings lead, each with real photos, the price, location, area and energy rating, and the areas covered and commission are facts stated the same everywhere. Take every listing detail from the owner or the listing documents; never invent or round up prices, areas, energy ratings, features or views, and never edit photos so that they mislead. Mark reserved properties and hide sold or let ones promptly. Never invent sales figures, "sold in X days" claims, awards, memberships, references or reviews, and never promise a price, a return on investment or a rise in value. Write neutrally and without discriminating wording. Whether the energy rating or other details must appear in a listing depends on local law – say it should be checked.
